scope: L1 materialization completion ordering, dependency-barrier and cancellation rollback reconciliation
window_size_policy: Every 0x400 window is acquisition coverage only. It is not an asserted function body size or semantic boundary.
non_claims: no separate fan-in counter is asserted
scheduler pending-entry rollback is not relabeled as OS AsyncIO cancellation
successful byte-window acquisition alone does not prove semantic equivalence
no original-process or Level-E receipt is produced by this plan

windows.purpose: Reacquire caller-owned-destination whole-file transfer submission and exact submit-failure/status behavior feeding the materialization completion boundary.
Reacquire callback(ticketId,userContext,errorFlag,bytesRead), byte-progress/status writes and the exact bridge from transport completion into higher materialization scheduling.
Reacquire the ReadRequest/FileSlot submission seam used by the whole-file transfer path; distinguish transport request ownership from the higher resource scheduler.
Reacquire pending scheduled-entry clear/rollback, queue matching and exact ordering. This is scheduler rollback evidence and must not be relabeled as OS-level AsyncIO cancellation.

Close the resource materialization submission/scheduling wrapper body, callees and inherited load-context consumption; test completion ordering and error propagation without assuming a fan-in counter.
Reacquire scheduler-ring enqueue slot metadata, callback/context writes, ring advancement and ordering relative to materialization submission and state2 completion.
Reacquire scheduler worker callback execution and slot-clear ordering to establish the materialization completion dependency barrier.
Reacquire exact cancellation sequence around scheduler rollback, state1/state2 to state4 writes and deferred cleanup enqueue.
Reacquire destination setup, materialization-dispatch success gate, state1 publication and state2-completion callback registration ordering.
Reacquire loose-container child submission/recursive in-place synthesis and determine whether child work introduces explicit completion dependencies or only ordered synchronous/scheduled calls.
Reacquire direct/packed/loose dispatch return semantics and its exact relationship to state1 publication and later completion scheduling.
Reacquire the resource-level completion callback, record-context decoding and exact conditions for state1 to state2 publication; this is not a raw I/O callback.
Reacquire deferred state4 cleanup and backing-release ordering to close the cancellation side of the completion barrier.
